title: One minute
body: Whatever starts today has to be small. Anything that starts big is up for negotiation by the second day; anything that starts small survives because it is boring.
action: Pick one thing that will take a minute, and do it today.

title: The second day
body: The first day happens on excitement. The second does not — because on the second day there is no excitement, only the work. Your chain really starts today.
action: Do the same as yesterday. No more than that.

title: The same hour
body: What you have to remember gets forgotten. What is tied to an hour is not remembered, it simply happens. Which hour does not matter; that it is the same one does.
action: Note today's hour. Tomorrow, the same hour.

title: The first resistance
body: Around the fourth day a thought comes: it would be fine to skip today. That is not a sign, it is only the newness running out. What is left when the newness goes is what we call a habit.
action: Do it today even if you do not feel like it. Keep it short, but do it.

title: The day you missed
body: Missing one day does not end a chain; saying "well, it is broken now" afterwards does. One day is a gap. Two is a decision.
action: If you missed it, come back today. Do not try to make it up — just carry on.

title: Somewhere visible
body: What is held in mind gets forgotten; what is in front of your eyes gets done. Most of what we call willpower is really a question of where you put things.
action: Put the thing where you will see it. The book on the pillow, the bottle on the desk.

title: A week
body: Seven days is enough to know whether something has taken with you. What changed is not you; it is that you no longer have to make the decision fresh each day.
action: What did you notice this week? Say it to yourself in one sentence.

title: Surroundings
body: What is hard in the same room, with the same people, at the same hour can get easier when the setting shifts a little. If you are struggling, it is not you that needs adjusting — it is the conditions.
action: Do the same thing somewhere else today, or in a different order.

title: The excuse sentence
body: Everyone has one: "I'm tired", "not today", "I'll make it up tomorrow". Recognising the sentence does not disarm it, but it does make it visible.
action: Write down your own excuse sentence. You will know it the next time you hear it.

title: Stop measuring
body: Constantly checking how far you have come is one of the things that slows the coming. Forget the counter today; it is counting anyway.
action: Do not measure how much you did today. Just do it.

title: The slowdown
body: The middle of the second week is where most things get quietly dropped. The reason is not failure, it is your attention moving elsewhere.
action: Halve the time today, but do not skip. The small version is the one that carries on.

title: Say it out loud
body: When you tell someone about a thing, two things happen: it gets clearer to you, and it gets harder to drop. The second one is the useful part.
action: Tell one person what you are doing. Not to boast — just to have said it.

title: What you will drop
body: Adding something new always takes the place of something. If you do not know what it replaced, that is the thing that will come back.
action: Notice what you have done less of over these thirteen days.

title: From here on
body: Fourteen days is not an ending, it is a measurement. What carries on from here is not an experiment any more. It is something you did.
action: If you are going to do it tomorrow, decide today. If you do not, tomorrow you will not be able to.
